ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AD \parallel BC$, $\angle B=35^\circ$, and $DB$ bisects $\angle ADE$, what is the measure of $\angle DEC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD\parallel BC$ and $\angle B=35^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle ADB=\angle B=35^\circ$, \\
Since DB bisects $\angle ADE$, \\
it follows that $\angle ADE=2\angle ADB=70^\circ$, \\
Since $AD\parallel BC$, \\
it follows that $\angle DEC =\angle ADE =\boxed{70^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Since $AD\parallel BC$ and $\angle B=35^\circ$, it follows that $\angle ADB=\angle B=35^\circ$. Since $DB$ bisects $\angle ADE$, $\angle ADE=2\angle ADB=70^\circ$. Since $AD\parallel BC$, $\angle DEC=\angle ADE=70^\circ$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a top horizontal segment AD and a lower horizontal line BC, with points B, E, C on the lower line in that order. Segment DB is drawn from B up to D, and segment DE is drawn from D down to E. The given condition states AD ∥ BC, ∠B = 35°, and DB bisects ∠ADE. Reasoning: Since DB intersects the parallel lines AD and BC, the angle between AD and DB at D equals the angle between BC and DB at B, so ∠ADB = ∠B = 35°. Because DB bisects ∠ADE, ∠ADE = 2 × ∠ADB = 70°. Since AD is parallel to EC (EC lies on BC), the angle made by DE with AD equals the corresponding angle made by DE with EC, hence ∠DEC = ∠ADE = 70°.
